Hi Ethan,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare to finalize the order form and MSA exhibits, Procurement and Security at Aperio asked me to confirm a few things around subprocessor flow-down and evidence so we can close legal review on our side. Can you confirm Redwood's approach on the following points?

- Will Redwood flow down the DPA obligations to any vendor that processes customer data on your behalf (encryption, restricted access, DSARs, breach notification)?
- For vendors in the chain that do not process customer data (e.g., monitoring, analytics), will you provide a written attestation and either SOC 2 link or equivalent controls evidence?
- What notice period do you provide for adding new subprocessors and is there an objection process?
- Can you commit to a published subprocessor inventory that we can reference in an order-form addendum?

Attached is a short 2-pager with our standard flow-down expectations (Aperio_SAAS_Security_Overview.pdf). We're on a tight timeline and would prefer minimal redlines to the MSA, and to handle anything specific in an Order Form Annex if possible.

Happy to jump on a short call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Jordan Hale
Head of Procurement | Aperio Cloud

Subject: Re: Subprocessor controls and flow-down for upcoming order form

Team —

I reviewed Aperio's questions and sketched out a concise redline approach so we don't reopen the full MSA. Key recommendations:

1) Flow-down trigger: Require flow-down of the DPA (security, breach notif, DSAR cooperation, data retention limits) to any subprocessor that "processes" Customer Data as defined in the DPA. For non-processing vendors, require written attestation and evidence.

2) Notice and objection: 30-calendar-day notice for new subprocessors; Customer may object within 14 calendar days with good-faith basis (e.g., access to cleartext sensitive data). If objection is raised, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to address.

3) Inventory / public list: Maintain a read-only subprocessor inventory URL in the Console and include a snapshot as an Order Form Annex. We will commit to daily updates for operational subprocessors, weekly for partner integrations.

4) Right to audit / evidence: For subprocessors that materially process Customer Data, require either (i) SOC 2 Type II report covering the relevant scope and within the last 12 months, or (ii) a completed security questionnaire and supporting evidence. For low-risk vendors, a signed attestation + point-in-time evidence is acceptable.

5) Encryption & access controls: Add explicit statement that Customer Data is encrypted at rest and in transit, and that access to production data is limited to named roles with least-privilege and just-in-time access logging.

6) DSAR & data residency: Flow-down to support DSARs and to honor regional residency restrictions where specified in the Order Form.

Operational notes attached in redline_summary.xlsx. I drafted clause text to insert into an Order Form Annex — we should use annex vs MSA where possible to keep enterprise customers comfortable.

I'll prepare a blackline for the MSA/Annex and circulate for review by EOD Monday. If Aperio can provide the SOC 2 report link now, we can fast-track.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
